tier_reason: Tier D stands (prose only); caveats corrected with the code-reading findings: swapped SetBounds arguments break non-square canvases, ScanT panics with 2 or more threads on unclipped geometry, and winding and clipping are unimplemented so the parity claim against ScanFT compares unequal work.

corrections.caveats: Prose claim only (ScanS at parity with ScanFT, ScanT faster with more threads), no numbers, ScanFT never timed. Code bugs: SetBounds(height, width) argument order swapped against rasterx callers, so non-square canvases paint wrong (all test SVGs are square); ScanT indexes cellWorkers with a negative value and panics when content reaches above the top edge with 2 or more threads; SetWinding and SetClip are no-ops, so no even-odd fill or clipping and counter-wound subpaths lose antialiasing. 1 star, abandoned since 2022-01-17; separate repo from the catalogued srwiley/scanx.

tier_reason: Tier C stands; caveats corrected: the measured mode is the approximate cached word-width path, not the exact mode the README advertises, and the wrapper breaks on UAX-29 word boundaries rather than UAX-14 line-break opportunities.

corrections.caveats: bench/compare.mjs (node-canvas, Apple Silicon, no CPU model or Node version, single run) times canvas-txt's default cached mode (summed per-word widths, no cross-word kerning) against canvas-hypertxt's exact standard mode; the exact mode (cache: false) is never benchmarked and only hypertxt's cache is cleared. 8.6x and 11.0x on never-repeating 600-char strings, but 0.9 vs 1.1 us/op on repeated text. Wrapping breaks on UAX-29 word segments, not UAX-14, so punctuation can start a line. canvas-hypertxt is catalogued.

tier_reason: Tier C stands; caveats corrected: the 2019 SpeedTestCV outputs compare unequal kernels and regions on the Sobel, contour and Hough rows, so only the mixed per-row picture survives.

corrections.caveats: SpeedTestCV outputs from commit 0bd58bd (2019-03-21; BoofCV 0.33.1 vs opencv-python 4.0.0.21, no hardware, JMH vs a Python time.time() loop): 5 rows faster, 3 slower (blur, Canny, mean threshold). The Sobel row uses OpenCV ksize=1 against BoofCV's 3x3 kernel, the contour row thresholds complementary regions, and the Hough row runs on a nearly all-non-zero 3648x2736 image, so those wins are not like for like. Java library, loose fit in color-and-resampling.

tier_reason: Tier C stands; caveats corrected: bm3dcuda now ships its own rolling temporal BM3Dv2 (R2.17, same author), the docs never say which bm3dcuda path was timed, and nssfactory's default bm_range 7 searches fewer candidates than bm3dcuda's 9.

corrections.caveats: First-party PR #23 numbers on an RTX 5080 (636 vs 732 fps, about 1.15x derived) with no timing harness, CPU, driver or bm3dcuda build stated; bm3dcuda has shipped its own rolling temporal BM3Dv2 since R2.17 (2026-09-26, same developer) and the docs do not say which bm3dcuda path was timed; nssfactory defaults to bm_range 7 against bm3dcuda's 9 and is built with IEEE flags while bm3dcuda's doc build uses --use_fast_math. Days-old work in progress, defaults changed within days, no released CUDA binary, 1 star, GPL-2.0-only.

tier_reason: Tier D stands (no first-party numbers); caveats corrected: the only published comparisons are user issues showing Simd slower than OpenCV on resize and colour conversion, and the current release carries an open heap-buffer-overflow report.

corrections.caveats: No published Simd vs OpenCV or libyuv numbers (ResizeOpenCvSpecialTest has no committed output; docs site blocked). The only third-party figures are unanswered issues where Simd loses: #149 upscale 9.789 ms vs OpenCV 4.5.1 3.689 ms (i7-10700), #212 Resize and BgrToGray 4-6x slower than OpenCV 4.5.5 (i7-10750H), thread counts unstated (Simd defaults to 1 thread, most resizers unparallelised). 8.0.166 removed several public APIs; open #299 ASan heap-buffer-overflow in an AVX-512 transpose and #274 illegal-instruction report. 2.3k stars, MIT, active.
